newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Mercury may have NGC stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Mercury may have NGC stake - paper.

text.p: Unlisted Mercury Energy is believed to have amassed about a four percent holding in Natural Gas Corp Ltd, the New Zealand Herald reported on Thursday.
Another energy company is also thought to have built a holding in the gas distributor, the paper said.
The emergence of the two shareholders on Natural Gas Corp's share register comes at a crucial time for the company as it progresses towards a potential capital reconstruction.

In October, about 420 million convertible notes mature. This could involve the reduction and payment of capital of up to NZ$210 million back to the note holders, which could be a prelude to a change in the shareholding structure of Natural Gas.

One broker in a client letter pointed to looming corporate activity. The higher dividend payout on the 42 million shares on issue that was recently announced effectively clears out the imputation credits held by the company and potentially paves the way for a change of ownership, it said.
Fletcher Energy and the Australian gas utility, AGL, each own a third of Natural Gas Corporation.
However, they are believed to have been uneasy partners since Natural Gas Corporation was formed and floated in 1992.
AGL has been expanding its operations in Australia. It is therefore viewed by some market analysts as a weak holder.
What Mercury's intentions might be is unclear. But Natural Gas Corporation is the supplier of gas to Mercury's new Southdown power station.
It will also supply the Stratford power station when it comes on steam. Mercury, along with TransAlta and Fletcher Energy, own Stratford.
